data.narrative:
Pyka is a Series B autonomous drone company founded by Michael Norcia, Chuma Ogunwole, Kyle Moore, and Nathan White. The company has raised $40M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of eight private companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector, including Elroy Air, Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, and Joby Aviation. No public comparables exist in this narrowly defined space.

Given the nascent stage of the sector and heterogeneity across peer business models, only one valuation method could be reliably applied. The stage-progression approach uses Pyka's $40M total raised as a proxy for current implied value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B progression to subsequent rounds, yielding $76M. A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data; applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the diversity of autonomous platforms and applications.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $65M to $87M (low to high), centered on $76M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include: the appropriate step-up multiplier for autonomous systems companies in a capital-intensive sector; the relevance of the heterogeneous peer set; and path-dependent risk factors specific to regulatory and commercialization timelines. Additional comparable transactions would strengthen conviction in this range.
